name: Industrial Parkway — Jerome Township 160 acres
availability: Currently advertised for sale/lease on broker page; live seller availability and option terms unconfirmed
powerClaim: Broker indexed highlights claim 50 MW via AEP/FirstEnergy, multiple fiber providers and by-right data-center zoning. These are marketing statements, not utility/authority confirmations. Delivered capacity is unknown.
utility: AEP/FirstEnergy/URE roles need parcel-specific reconciliation; broker references multiple systems.
matchRationale: Cologix and 365 have Columbus-region development signals; metro connectivity and a 160-acre expansion footprint are a more specific fit than rural acreage alone.
EdgeConneX could evaluate a customer-led Ohio campus; no open mandate verified.
Google is a regional self-builder, but the marketed 50 MW first block is not proof of a Google capacity requirement.
blockers: APNs, legal description and offered tract boundaries not yet obtained.
Actual tariff, collateral, deliverability and expansion beyond advertised first phase require utility confirmation.
Broker entitlement claim needs adopted approvals and site-plan verification.
Ohio paused new tax-exemption requests; this is not a statewide development ban. Local restrictions still need separate checking.
Option fee/purchase price may be incompatible with founder limits.

sources.title: Ohio pause of new data-center tax exemptions, not a ban

name: Lot 1 Connect 470 — Aurora 26.8 acres
address: E Jewell Avenue at S Gun Club Road, Aurora, Colorado 80018
availability: Listing expressly says currently available; contact JLL. No seller-confirmed option availability.
powerClaim: No verified MW. Brochure substation proximity is not capacity.
matchRationale: 365 explicitly named Aurora in its May 2026 development pipeline, making the geography a real match; its existing LOI could also mean demand is already allocated.
Cologix and H5 have Denver-area ecosystems, but acquisition appetite for this suburb is unverified.
Broker concepts of a 249,480 square-foot building and up to 400,000 square feet describe potential development, not an existing delivered building.
blockers: The 26.8-acre Lot 1 is not the entire 173.1-acre Connect 470 offering; do not combine acreage or assume assemblage.
Bare-land delivery may miss 365’s conversion-led schedule.
Airport District zoning is advertised; exact data-center use approval and aviation constraints need authority review.
Deliverable MW, diverse fiber paths, APN and water capacity are unverified.

name: 3101 NW 128th Street — Kansas City 163 acres
priceText: $8,999,950; record also lists $55,000 per acre (rounded). Reconfirm price.
availability: KC SmartPort states for sale; record updated October 19, 2026
powerClaim: Listing says adjacent to new substation, Evergy service, utilities available. No capacity verified or implied.
utility: Evergy per marketing record; exact parcel service confirmation absent
matchRationale: Marketing record claims contiguity to Meta and Google technology parks; if boundaries prove it, this supports an expansion/assemblage hypothesis tied to named users.
163 acres is below Meta’s typical 500-acre co-op RFI; only adjacent expansion or a larger assemblage would resolve the mismatch.
Lincoln has a land-partner development model; Lightedge has Kansas City demand, although this tract is much larger than its recent 3 MW acquisition.
blockers: Need official parcel map and title to verify claimed contiguity and owner.
Existing campuses may already have adequate expansion land and power rights.
Nearly $9 million asking price exceeds founder fee-simple resources; affordable assignable control has not been offered.
No written utility MW/ramp, diverse fiber routes, use approval or environmental clearance.

name: NG Data Center — Chester, Virginia
availability: JLL currently advertises whole-property sale or floor leases; seller confirmation still needed
powerClaim: No current delivered or expansion MW established in the opened broker listing.
matchRationale: Existing data-center structure is closer to TierPoint, H5 and 365 acquisition/reuse precedents than a raw-land option.
Chester/Richmond provides a Mid-Atlantic location; local customer, fiber and network economics still require confirmation.
DāSTOR is an exploratory regional expansion prospect, not a verified Richmond buyer.
blockers: The listing headline says 193,055 square feet while sale prose says 192,595; reconcile exact area.
No plant-condition, firm power, tenant/vacancy or sale-price evidence reviewed.
Must establish reuse economics and ability to support the buyer’s actual liquid-cooling/rack-density target.
Existing facility purchase is a different transaction from small land-option origination; founder should seek buyer-backed exclusivity only.

name: Silver Spring colocation data center — expansion/acquisition lead
address: Silver Spring, Maryland; exact offered address must be reconciled with broker (not assumed from similarly named facilities)
availability: JLL advertises fee-simple sale on behalf of Sansone Group and Priseda; no seller contact made
powerClaim: Broker reports 18 MW contracted IT load, two 9 MW Pepco feeds and additional capacity opportunities. Do not add redundant feeds or equate contracted load with currently delivered independent MW. Future-feed timing in listing requires refresh.
utility: Pepco per broker; service rights and ramp require provider documents
matchRationale: Operating, leased colocation infrastructure with unused data-hall space fits facility-acquisition and expansion strategies.
H5/Netrality would require evidence of network ecosystem; TierPoint/Lightedge would require customer retention, compliance and retrofit economics.
This is an acquisition/expansion comparable and partnership lead, not a cheap vacant parcel or an empty facility awaiting first construction.
blockers: Exact address, parcels and offering perimeter need broker confirmation.
Current tenant commitments and redundancy changes limit free capacity.
Broker calls facility Tier IV while describing N+1 reconfiguration; certification/design claims need engineering review.
Price and institutional capital requirements probably exceed founder-only execution; control/assignment terms unknown.
Build probability must mean incremental expansion/retrofit, not initial facility construction, which has already occurred.

sources.title: JLL Silver Spring Data Center sale offering
